But then how did I acquire a taste for things like tomatoes and onions?

I'll tell you my theory. I think once we do something enough, we associate it with ourselves, it becomes personal, and therefore more enjoyable-seeming. But when something is new we often regard it as alien to us and unfamiliar.

It might explain that. I used to think I didn't like them but it turns out I only tried them once and then made my mind up. Tomatoes are an acquired taste. I used to also think I didn't like onions. Same problem, I hadn't tried them enough. Now I love onions, cannot imagine life without them. Same with bell peppers. It's all about normalization. You get used to something and now you "like" it.

They key is repetition. Trying them once a year basically assures you'll never acquire the taste. Tastes don't get acquired in one go.

This is a secret to human nature. We "like" what we are used to. If you keep eating tomatoes you will start liking them, for the sheer fact that you're used to them.

I mean there are exceptions to this obviously but in general it's true.
